artboards.title: Presets as it stands today — nine faults, and the six doors that say nothing
Proposed — nothing left unset, a counter login, and a save that did not land
Proposed — The shop: three regions, no doors, and a band that names what is unset

annotations.text:
WHAT YOU SETTLED, AND WHAT FOLLOWS FROM IT

You answered four questions before I drew. Everything here follows from them.

1. RE-ARCHITECT THE IA. So the twelve sub-tabs are gone, the page is renamed, and three of its panes are argued into a different shape. Nothing has moved off the page — every setting that was on Presets is still here.

2. A CLICKABLE PROTOTYPE. Main works. Type in the search field and regions appear and disappear; add and delete words in any of the five lists; set the default price rule and watch the amber band lose that clause and the index row turn from "not set" to "set"; set an order limit and watch "none of 6" count up; switch mobile money to Production and it asks first. The rest is drawn, not wired.

3. DESKTOP ONLY, AT 1440. There is no phone artboard here. What today's page does at 390 — the twelve-item nav becomes a horizontal scrolling strip and the five group labels are set to display:none — is the worst thing on the screen, and it is a whole second design. It is the open question at the end of this canvas, not something I have quietly answered.

4. OWNER AND ADMINS AND STAFF. So permission is drawn, not assumed: three regions, three audiences, and a locked region that says what it is rather than vanishing.

Everything is drawn from index.html's own values — the 23-colour palette, the 11/12/13/14 ramp, Inter + Archivo Black + IBM Plex Mono, and the .ow-* console components already shipping on Products, Inventory, Debtors and Today. No new colour, no new weight, no new type size, no fourteenth button family. Nothing in index.html has changed: this is the drawing.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT AS IT STANDS >

Read out of index.html — the markup at lines 16395–16732, its CSS at 2179–2250, and the wiring at 63672 and 64140–64340. Nothing here is invented.

1. THE NAME IS WRONG FOR HALF THE PAGE. A preset is a value that pre-fills a field. That describes six of the twelve panes. Order timing is a policy that drives an alert; Mobile money is a live merchant credential store; Signed-in devices is a security surface that changes by the hour; Shop identity is what prints on paper. An owner hunting for "where do I turn off automatic printing" does not think "presets", and the nav's own keywords admit it: settings categories units defaults options.

2. TWELVE DOORS, AND SIX OF THEM SAY NOTHING. The nav puts a count on the six word lists. The other six carry no state at all — .pset-count:empty{display:none}. So you cannot tell from the nav whether the shop has a name, whether a default price rule exists, whether any order limit is set, or whether mobile money is live. The six that say nothing are the six that matter.

3. THE PAGE NEVER MENTIONS THAT AN UNSET SETTING IS BREAKING ANOTHER SCREEN. presetDefaultMarkup defaults to {}. A product with no rule of its own and no shop default cannot be quoted, sold at the counter, or catalogued — the Products register already ships a mark for exactly this state, and it fires because of a blank on THIS page. This page does not say so anywhere.

4. THREE WAYS TO SAVE, ON ONE SCREEN, WITH NO RULE. Shop identity writes on every keystroke, silently (64165). Agent terms write on change with a toast (64207). Mobile money has two explicit "Save MTN settings" / "Save Airtel settings" buttons. The code comment at 64148 says there is no apply step anywhere else here — that stopped being true when the mobile-money pane landed on the page, and nobody updated it. An owner has no way to know whether a number took.

5. LIVE PAYMENT CREDENTIALS ARE ONE CLICK FROM A LIST OF UNITS. MTN and Airtel merchant keys and a sandbox→production switch sit as the seventh item in the same flat nav as Units and Locations. The pane's own prose says credentials are readable by owners and admins only, but nothing on screen shows a permission, and flipping Environment to Production — which starts debiting real phones — is an ordinary <select> with no confirmation.

6. FIVE SHOP-WIDE RULES ARE NOT ON THIS PAGE AT ALL. Restock cover (buy_cover, on What to buy), target margin and dead-after (pr_target / pr_days, on Pricing), chase-after days (chase_after, on Chase debts) and price-watch days (pw_days, on the Price registry) all write to the same presets blob this page owns. There is no single place to see what the app assumes.

7. THE PROSE COMES BEFORE THE CONTROL. Default price rule opens with 87 words, Mobile money with 76, before the first field. The house pattern is one line in .ow-ph-sub with the rest folded behind the "i"; this page prints everything inline, so on several panes the thing you came for is below the fold of its own pane.

8. FORTY-ONE SETTINGS AND NO SEARCH. Finding one means guessing which of twelve doors it is behind.

9. THE ACCENT IS EVERYWHERE. The house law is one oxide element per screen. This page has the active tab (oxide-soft ground, oxide text), every .pset-group h4 in oxide, and two .btn-accent Save buttons — before counting the rail. When everything is marked, nothing is.

AND OFF THE DRAWING:

10. IT IS A LEGACY SCREEN. .page-head, .panel, .pset-* — while Products, Inventory, Debtors and Today next door speak .ow-ph / .ow-pan / .ow-grid / .ow-lr.

11. THE PHONE IS THE DESKTOP NARROWED. At 820px the nav becomes a horizontal scroller and .pset-nav-group is display:none — so the five group names, which are the only thing telling you what the twelve doors have to do with each other, are deleted on the surface with the least room to guess.

THE PROPOSAL — what changed, and why

THE PAGE IS RENAMED "THE SHOP". Not Presets, not Settings. The page's actual subject is one thing: everything the app assumes about this shop until told otherwise. The sub-line says exactly that. It sits in the Setup group beside Staff, and it reads the way this app's other screens read — The day, Manager, Analysis. Keywords are unchanged, so search still finds it by "presets", "settings", "units", "defaults".

TWELVE DOORS BECOME NONE. Three regions on one scroll: THE WORDS THE SHOP USES, THE RULES IT WORKS BY, THE SHOP ITSELF. That grouping is not cosmetic — it is the three genuinely different kinds of thing that were jammed together. A word list decides what a field suggests and costs nothing if it is wrong. A rule changes what other screens compute and warn about tomorrow. The shop's identity, its merchant keys and its sessions carry legal and financial exposure. They deserve different treatments, different permissions, and different amounts of ceremony — which is impossible while they are twelve identical pills.

THE BAND NAMES WHAT IS UNSET AND WHAT DEPENDS ON IT. "3 settings are unset, and something depends on each" — then one line each: no default price rule and 23 lines fall through it; no shop name and 1,204 receipts have gone out anonymous; no order limits and the alert has never fired. A decomposition, not a badge: it says which and how many, so it can be argued with. It is the same grammar the Products register already ships. And it is ABSENT — not empty, not a green tick — when there is nothing unset. The accent lives here and nowhere else on the page, because this is the one thing to do next.

THE SIX WORD LISTS ARE ON ONE SCREEN INSTEAD OF BEHIND SIX DOORS. They are all the same shape — a list of strings you add, rename and delete — so a door each was six doors to see one kind of thing. Every list carries its count and the one sentence saying where its words appear. The add field sits inline at the end of the chips, so adding a category is: click, type, Enter. Rename is a click on the word. Delete is one × instead of a pencil AND an ×, which halves the controls on a page that had 57 of them.

THE RULES BECOME ROWS THAT STATE THEIR CONSEQUENCE. Each is a name, one line of what it drives, and its control — not a pane of prose with a number at the bottom. "Trust a price for 90 days" says it drives Prices to check on Analysis. "Prices to check each month" says 41 are currently older than the window. The rule and the thing it does are on the same line, which is the whole reason the prose existed and the reason it can now be one line instead of five.

AND THE FIVE RULES SET ELSEWHERE ARE LISTED HERE. Restock cover, target margin, dead-after, chase-after, price-watch: shown with their current values and a door to the screen that sets them. They stay set there, beside the figures they change, so a number is never altered without its consequence on screen — but they are READ here, which is what makes this page the whole answer to "what does the app assume?".

PERMISSION IS DRAWN. Counter and picker logins see the words. Admins see the words and the rules. Owners see all three regions. A locked region is shown locked and says what it is — "This shop takes MTN Mobile Money, and it is live" — because a picker who cannot find mobile money concludes the shop does not take it and tells a customer so.

GOING LIVE ON MOBILE MONEY ASKS FIRST. It is the one action on the page that is not autosave, and the only place a second .btn-accent appears, inside its own confirmation. Everything else saves the moment you leave a field: one grammar for the whole page, replacing three.

THE INDEX REPLACES THE NAV, AND CARRIES STATE ON EVERY ROW. Fourteen rows, each with its value — 7, 12, "not set", "none of 6", "MTN live". It is a map, not a set of tabs: nothing is hidden behind it. Clicking a row searches for it. This is the single thing the old nav could not do for half its entries.

THE SEARCH IS THE PRIMARY NAVIGATION FOR ANYONE WHO HAS BEEN HERE BEFORE. Forty-one settings, one field, and it matches what a setting DOES rather than what the app calls it — "receipt" finds three things, none of which is named receipt.

THE THREE STATES >

1. NOTHING LEFT UNSET. The band is gone. Not an empty band, not a green tick, not "all set ✓". A settings page that congratulates you for filling it in teaches you to scroll past the top of it — and then the day it has something real to say, you scroll past that too. Two order steps are deliberately left blank and the page does not argue: Loaded and Delivered wait on a lorry and a customer, not on this shop. Blank is an answer, so "4 of 6" is ink, not amber.

2. A COUNTER LOGIN OPENS THE SAME PAGE. Three locked panels, each saying what it is: the shop takes MTN and it is live; this is what prints on your receipts; your own device is on the signed-in list. Locked rather than hidden, and the index still lists all three regions with a count of how many of the 41 are yours. A map that hides the rooms you cannot enter is a map you stop trusting.

3. ONE WORD TYPED, AND A SAVE THAT DID NOT LAND. "receipt" matches three settings and nothing on the page is named receipt — the search indexes what a setting does. The words and the rules did not match, so neither region is drawn, and the page does not report "0 results" about regions nobody asked for.

THE FAILED WRITE IS THE STATE THAT DOES NOT EXIST TODAY. Shop identity writes on every keystroke with no acknowledgement of any kind, so a dropped connection is completely silent: you type the new address, it looks saved because it is in the box, and receipts keep printing the old one. Here the failure names itself where the change was made, keeps your value in the field, says what still works and what does not, and — the part that matters — the receipt preview shows what is ON FILE rather than echoing the box. A preview that echoed the box would have confirmed the change had landed.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DECIDED FOR YOU

1. THE NAME. "The shop" is a proposal, and it is the one change here that touches other people's muscle memory. It is one nav label, one data-tab value and one page title; the keywords stay, so search still answers to "presets". If you would rather it stayed Presets, everything else on this canvas still stands — the name is the only thing that depends on it.

2. WHETHER THE FIVE OUTSIDE RULES SHOULD BE EDITABLE HERE. I have drawn them read-only with a door, because each one currently sits beside the figures it changes and moving it here would mean changing a number with no idea what it does to the list in front of you. The opposite argument is real: an owner setting the shop up wants to set all eleven rules in one sitting. Making them editable in both places is the third option and my least favourite — two controls for one number is how they drift.

3. WHETHER MOBILE MONEY AND SIGNED-IN DEVICES BELONG ON THIS PAGE AT ALL. You said nothing moves off, so nothing has. But merchant credentials and live sessions are not "what the app assumes about this shop" — they are how it connects to the outside world and who is holding a key to it. If a Security page is ever worth having, those two are its content, and this page loses its only two owners-only panels.

4. HOW LONG THE PAGE IS. Everything on one scroll is about 3,700px. I think that is right for a page with a search field and an index — nothing is hidden, and Ctrl-F works, which it cannot when content lives behind a tab. But it is a real cost and the honest alternative is to collapse the three regions and remember which was open.

5. RENAME BY CLICKING THE WORD, WITH NO PENCIL. The current chip carries a pencil AND an ×. Dropping the pencil halves 57 controls and removes 57 chances to hit delete when you meant edit; the cost is that renaming is now discoverable only from the line of copy under the lists. If that trade is wrong, the pencil comes back and the page grows 57 controls again.

6. THE FIGURES IN THE BAND ARE ILLUSTRATIVE. 23 lines falling through the default rule, 1,204 anonymous receipts, 41 stale prices — each is derivable from data the app already holds, and none is computed yet. If any one of them cannot be derived cheaply, the rule is to say so rather than show a number: "some lines" is not an option, "not counted" is.

7. THE PHONE. Not drawn, because you scoped this to the desktop. What is there today is not a phone design — it is the desktop with its nav turned sideways and its five group labels deleted. When you want it, it is its own piece of work, and my instinct is that the phone's job here is only the words and the search: an owner does not set a merchant API key in a yard.

8. WHAT I HAVE NOT TOUCHED. No preset is read, written or computed differently. Every value, default and fallback in the presets blob is exactly as it is today. This is the same data, saved the same way, drawn differently — plus one thing that is new and is not a drawing decision: the failed-write state in artboard 3, which the page needs whatever you think of the rest of this.
